title: Fine-tune Qwen 3 on a custom dataset
description: Fine-tune Qwen 3 8B on a custom ShareGPT dataset with Soup CLI. YAML config, multi-turn training, and vLLM serving walkthrough.

blocks.html:
Fine-tune Qwen 3 on a custom dataset

Qwen 3 is one of the strongest open-weight models for reasoning and multilingual tasks. This guide shows how to fine-tune Qwen 3 8B on your own dataset with Soup CLI.

1. Install

Since v0.71.0 the base soup-cli package is a light, PyTorch-free CLI. [train] adds the training stack; [fast] adds Unsloth on top. Installing [fast] alone cannot train. Since v0.77.0 Soup needs Python 3.11 to 3.13 (>=3.11,<3.14); on Python 3.10, pip keeps installing v0.76.x.

2. Dataset (ShareGPT format)

Qwen 3 handles multi-turn conversations well. Use the ShareGPT format:

That one row only shows the shape of the file. Soup holds out 10% of the rows for validation by default (data.val_split), so a one-row file leaves nothing to train on (soup train --dry-run on it exits 1 with No training rows). Use your real dataset.

3. Config

blocks.code:
base: Qwen/Qwen3-8B
task: sft
backend: unsloth            # root-level, NOT under training

data:
  train: conversations.json
  format: sharegpt
  max_length: 4096          # sequence length lives under data

training:
  epochs: 2
  lr: 1.5e-4                # the key is lr, not learning_rate
  batch_size: 4
  gradient_accumulation_steps: 4
  gradient_checkpointing: true   # since v0.77.0 the default false turns Unsloth's off
  lora:
    r: 32                   # LoRA turns on when r > 0; there is no enabled flag
    alpha: 64
    target_modules: [q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj, gate_proj, up_proj, down_proj]

output: ./runs/qwen3

blocks.html:
Why target all projections? Qwen 3 benefits from training LoRA on both attention and MLP projections for instruction-following tasks.

Why gradient_checkpointing: true is spelled out (v0.77.0, #1981). Through v0.76.x the Unsloth backend always used Unsloth's own checkpointing kernel, whatever the config said. Since v0.77.0 it honours training.gradient_checkpointing, and the schema default false turns checkpointing off, which uses more activation memory at max_length: 4096. true keeps Unsloth's kernel, as every earlier release used.

Before you train

Save the config as qwen3.yaml and run soup doctor --config qwen3.yaml first. Since v0.76.0 many more settings are refused when the config loads, each naming the field and what to change, so a config that loaded on an older release can stop loading. soup doctor --config prints the error and exits 2 without loading a model (it stops at the first cross-field refusal, so fix that setting and run it again until it prints no error), and since v0.77.0 it no longer prints All checks passed! above a refusal. Several things v0.76 only warned about are refused at v0.77.0, for example a staged field (validated, read by nothing) set away from its default, which stops the load with a line ending refused as of v0.77. Delete the line., and the deprecated data.remove_unused_columns: true. See Config refusals.

4. Train

In a script or CI job, pass --yes: since v0.77.0 soup train with its stdin piped or redirected and no --yes exits 3 instead of waiting at the confirmation prompt.

5. Serve with vLLM

Pass the adapter directory itself as --model: Soup reads the base model from its adapter_config.json and serves base plus LoRA. --adapters name=path (several adapters on one server) is for --backend transformers only and exits 1 with --backend vllm.

The model is now available at http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions with OpenAI-compatible API.

Tips

  • Qwen 3 has a vocabulary of about 151k tokens, so the output logits are large. If a run runs out of memory, lower data.max_length or training.batch_size before anything else.
  • training.neftune_alpha: 5 adds noise to the embeddings during training (NEFTune). Whether it helps depends on your data; compare against a run without it.
  • training.packing: true packs several short examples into one sequence for efficient training on short data. Upstream reports that on TRL 0.29.1 a packed SFT run lost the assistant-only labels and trained every input token except the first, prompt and system tokens included; since v0.76.0 packing keeps the assistant-only loss mask (#1236). If you packed with assistant-only masking on, check which TRL you had.
